output_json.patch_notes: Extracted the archive-extraction loop from copyDirectoryFromPod into a package-private method extractArchiveFromPod(InputStream, Path) so the extraction logic can be unit-tested without a live pod/process. Inside that method, before writing each entry, the code computes the canonical destination directory once and, for every entry, resolves f = new File(destinationDir, entry.getName()).getCanonicalFile(). If the canonical target is not the destination directory itself and does not start with destinationDir + File.separator, an IOException ("Entry is outside of the target directory") is thrown, blocking traversal via "../" sequences and absolute paths. Legitimate nested entries (e.g. "sub/file.txt") still extract normally. Added two regression tests in CopyTest: testExtractArchiveRejectsPathTraversal (builds a base64/gzip/tar stream with a "../evil.txt" entry, asserts IOException and that no file escapes the destination) and testExtractArchiveExtractsLegitimateEntries (asserts a normal nested entry extracts). All 4 CopyTest tests pass and the build succeeds.
output_json.risk_notes: The fix uses getCanonicalFile(), which resolves symlinks; if the destination directory itself legitimately contains symlinked subdirectories pointing elsewhere, extraction into those targets would now be rejected — an unlikely and arguably desirable behavior for this security control. The public API and normal (non-malicious) extraction behavior are unchanged. The refactor moves the post-extraction proc.waitFor() status check to run after extractArchiveFromPod returns, preserving original ordering. No dependency or formatting changes beyond the touched methods.
output_json.summary: Fixed a CWE-022 path-traversal ("tar slip") vulnerability in Copy.copyDirectoryFromPod. Untrusted tar entry names from the pod (e.g. "../../etc/passwd") were joined to the destination directory and written without validation, allowing files to be written outside the intended directory. The extraction loop now resolves each entry's canonical path and rejects any entry that does not stay inside the destination directory.
